note: He is the purest expression of good-to-great in this batch and the clearest failure of the other half of the definition. On starting point he is ideal: 28, lifelong athlete, no pain, no injuries, self-rated seven out of ten and wanting the ten, with the ambition framed as a disposition rather than a fix — 'I'm at peace where I am now, and I'm just excited to up-level forever.' He fails 'successful' as stated: a life coach and breathwork facilitator early in building his practice, supported by a caregiving day job, is not the business owner or physician archetype. He also fails 'neglected_health' outright, and in the opposite direction to everyone else in this batch — health is his most invested area, not his least: 'I would say I actually have great health and fitness... there's not really any big pain points.' Income is omitted from both arrays rather than guessed, because it was never tested: no coaching price was quoted and no financial question was asked. Taken with the Dylan call in the same file, that is now two prospects in one recording whose affordability was assumed rather than established, and in both cases the assumption removed the offer.
